newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia wins two Hong Kong network orders.
newsitem.headline: Nokia wins two Hong Kong network orders.

text.p: Finnish telecoms group Nokia Oy said in a statement on Tuesday it won orders for PCN (Personal Communication Network) networks from two Hong Kong operators.
One of the contracts, with P Plus Communications, was worth nearly 150 million markka, Nokia said in the statement.
The value of the other agreement, with New World PCS, would not be disclosed, a Nokia spokeswoman said by telephone, adding the contract was "significant".
"Nokia Telecommunications ... has signed agreements with two Honk Kong PCN operators ... for the supply of PCS (DCS 1800) networks to Hong Kong," it said.

Both P Plus -- a consortium led by Star Telecom, Pacific Electrical Wire and Cable Group of Taiwan and Telecom Finland -- and New World PCS -- part of Hong Kong's New World Telephone Holdings -- are new PCS (Personal Communication Services) license operators in Hong Kong, Nokia said.
"The award of PCS licenses will help Hong Kong to meet growing demand for digital mobile phone service," it said.
The number of mobile phone users in Hong Kong was expected to rise to 1.2 million by the end of 1996 from 700,000 at the beginning of this year, Nokia said.
The contracts with both operators included the switching platform, base stations, base station controllers and the network management system, it said.
